duplicate_shadow_check: PASS. The Project machine remains the only transition authority: control.registry.project calls evaluate() and declares no transition table, surfaces.command declares no lifecycle state literal, and the frontend is forbidden by executable control from naming a canonical state as a whole token or declaring any relation-shaped identifier. GET /api/lifecycle/project publishes the machine's state vocabulary only - transitions, forbidden and terminal are deliberately never published, asserted by a negative control - so no client can decide legality for itself. Policy authority is likewise single: no operation class from the canonical vocabulary, no TRUST tier and no PDP/PEP identifier appears in frontend production source. Persistence is single: no browser store is used, and the transport types are compared field by field against the live OpenAPI document rather than maintained as a second model.
security_findings: None open. Every Command Center route enforces through the Phase 4 PEP - READ_FILE for reads, WRITE_WORKSPACE_FILE for writes - and a control parses the deployed source and fails if any route skips the guard, so a new unguarded endpoint cannot become a silent bypass. WRITE_STABLE_FILE and ROLLBACK_STABLE are never requested by this surface and both remain DENY to its actor. Refusal bodies carry only a stable code and the domain message: no filesystem path, no database URL, no ORM object, no traceback, no dialect name and no secret-shaped field, each asserted by a negative control. A refused write is proven absent after a restart. lifecycle.recovery is Protected Core and was changed, so the stronger verification profile applies and its three categories were executed.
fake_success_scan: Clean. Structure validator checks 9-12 PASS. No capability is claimed from the existence of a file: the ARK-REQ-0229 control asserts each link against the thing it links to and proves the runtime chain by writing through HTTP, discarding the application, and reading the row back through a separate engine. The first version of that control was vacuous - it searched the whole module graph for each client operation and found them in the client that declares them - and a mutation removing the page's transition call did not fail it; that was found by mutation testing, fixed, and recorded in DECISION_LOG.md. Every control added in this phase was mutation-tested before being relied on. T10 is real and its harness is itself controlled: an in-memory database, an intercepted route or a substituted application fails test_browser_journey_integrity.py. The 23 jsdom component tests are recorded as component evidence and are nowhere offered as browser E2E.
limitations: T10 covers one capability - the Project Registry - in Chromium only. Firefox and WebKit are not installed and no cross-browser claim is made. The journey runs on loopback against a locally served build; there is no packaged-release or clean-environment evidence (T14, Phase 36). Backup/restore is MINIMAL: no Recovery Supervisor (Phase 22B), no ROLLBACK_STABLE, which the PDP denies for every actor, and no cross-schema-revision restore - a restore requires an exactly matching schema revision rather than migrating across one (Phase 20). Python is 3.12.10, not the canonical 3.13; no Python lockfile exists because no lock tool is present; ruff and hypothesis are absent, so the T6 property tier is NOT_CONFIGURED. Rust/Tauri is UNSUPPORTED on this host. Five of the six canonical execution surfaces do not exist, so end-to-end bypass resistance across all six (ARK-REQ-0325, 0347) remains Phase 31 and is not claimed. provenance_ref is a nullable reference: content-addressed revision identity is Phase 6.
